title: Find retiring AI model IDs in your code
excerpt: SunsetLint is a GitHub App that finds retiring AI model IDs in your repos, with file, line and the shutdown date.
content_html:
GitHub App

Find retiring AI model IDs in your code, with file and line, before the shutdown date

Provider notices tell you which model is retiring. SunsetLint

tells

you

where it is: the file and line in each repository, next to the shutdown date and the replacement the provider recommends.

See it in 30 seconds

The next deadline

Anthropic announced on 30 September 2026 that Claude Sonnet 4.5 retires on 30 November 2026. Source:

Anthropic model deprecations, last verified

6 October 2026

.

StatusIdentifierProviderDateDetails
RetiringClaude Sonnet 4.5Anthropic30 Nov 2026What to change
SunsetAssistants APIOpenAI26 Aug 2026Find leftover calls
Rejected (HTTP 400)temperature / top_p / top_kAnthropic, Claude 4.7+In effectWhy it breaks

Why a scanner, not another feed

How it will work

What happens after you install the App.

  1. 1

    Install on your GitHub org

    Pick all repositories or a few. The App asks for read-only access to contents and cannot change code.

  2. 2

    Scan against verified rules

    Each rule is an identifier pattern with the provider's shutdown date, the replacement and a link to the notice. A person checks each rule before it ships.

  3. 3

    One issue per repository

    A rolling issue lists file:line, identifier, shutdown date, replacement and source. It updates as you fix things.

  4. 4

    Checks on pull requests (Pro)

    A Check Run annotates pull requests that add a new reference to a retiring identifier, so old IDs don't creep back in.

What it doesn't do

  • It doesn't open pull requests or edit code. It has no write access to contents.
  • It doesn't guarantee complete coverage. It checks your code against the rules we have verified, and each rule links to its source.
  • It doesn't support GitLab or Bitbucket.

Find retiring model IDs in your repositories

Install the GitHub App on your account and choose repositories. The first scan runs straight away and posts what it matched as an issue, with the file, line, shutdown date and source.
